correctness.rationale: For each received word y, form its exact set of source subsequences (insertions) or supersequences (deletions). A code C is list-two admissible exactly when the intersection with every received-word incidence set has size at most 2, equivalent to avoiding all three-codeword forbidden triples. The supplied source has a complete constant-popcount enumeration at the optimum k and next k+1 over every binary codebook at n=2..5; the second source implementation independently computes three-word common shortest supersequence / longest common subsequence rather than incidence masks. Crucially, downward closure turns absence at k+1 into impossibility of all larger codes. I independently implemented a third C++ forbidden-hypergraph enumerator and checked each of eight optima/next-level counts exactly, obtaining the stated labeled-optimum vectors. A separate independent group-action calculation of the 185 insertion optima yields 41 orbits size four, ten size two, and one singleton. For n=5 all 32 codewords, 128 insertion outputs, and 8 deletion outputs are covered; there is no infinite-length inference.

value.rationale: This is the first natural finite separation of equal-error-budget insertion and deletion list-two code capacities, together with a complete extremizer census rather than a lone witness. Exact small-blocklength examples are relevant test cases for emerging list-decoding conversion/capacity results; the 52 orbit types expose structure not captured by asymptotic rates. Its finite nature is deliberate and not a weakness by itself.

final_claim: For binary words length n=2,3,4,5 with list bound 2 after exactly two insertions or exactly two deletions, optimal code sizes are D=(2,3,4,4) and I=(2,3,4,6). Numbers of labeled optima are deletion (6,6,33,3089), insertion (6,6,43,185). At n=5 the insertion 185 optima occupy 52 reversal-and-complement orbits of sizes 4 x41, 2 x10, 1 x1; n=5 is first same-budget separation.
